newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac to address Palestinian council, revive port.
newsitem.headline: Chirac to address Palestinian council, revive port.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac will become the first foreign leader to address the Palestinian Legislative Council next week during a six-day tour of the tense Middle East region, diplomats said.
Seeking to assert a greater French and European role in the region, Chirac will address the 88-member assembly in the West Bank town of Ramallah next Wednesday.
He will then fly with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to the Gaza Strip, visit a refugee camp and lay a foundation stone for a disputed Gaza sea port, they said.
The French president will be the second European leader to lay a stone for the uncertain $60 million project on the Gaza coastline, stymied by Israeli security objections.

Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok laid the first stone in January. The Netherlands is the biggest donor in the project with $25 million to France's $20 million. Germany will donate the remaining $15 million.

Palestinian and Israeli sources said that although the port was agreed in Israeli-PLO peace accords, the Israelis have objected to it on security grounds, since it would give the Palestinians uncontrolled access to the sea.

The sources say Israel could also have economic and political motives for blocking the port, since Palestinan goods are currently forced to transit through Israel's port of Ashdod, giving the Jewish state valuable control.
A hasty attempt by Arafat's Palestinian Authority to build a smaller marina for Gaza fishermen foundered in 1994, shortly after Arafat returned from exile, wrecked by winter storms.
A mangled, rusting pier near Arafat's beachfront office is all that remains.
Chirac will spend a day in the Palestinian self-rule areas after visiting Syria on Saturday and Sunday, and Israel on Monday and Tuesday.
A French diplomat said Chirac's tour was the most difficult foreign trip of his 18 months in office.
He would seek a political role for the European Union in Middle East peace talks despite objections from the United States and Israel.

The Europeans were excluded from this month's emergency Arab-Israeli summit in Washington and U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher wrote to EU leaders urging them to stay out of the Israeli-Palestinian negotiations, diplomats said.
The French argue that the EU is the main financial sponsor of the peace process and can offer useful proposals and good offices without supplanting Washington as mediator.

But to avoid a clash with hardline Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, neither Chirac nor French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette would visit Orient House in Arab East Jerusalem, the PLO's unofficial headquarters in the city, the sources said.
After the Palestinian territories, Chirac will make brief visits to Jordan, Lebanon and Egypt on October 24-25.
